title: Taxi drivers rarely die of Alzheimer's — how complex mental maps protect your brain
description: The Conversation reports that taxi drivers' complex spatial navigation skills provide protection against Alzheimer's. Behavioral economics angle: how cognitive reserve and complex mental mapping act as buffers against neurodegeneration.
notes: Spatial reasoning and complex mental maps — skills sharpened by navigating London-style streets — provide neuroprotective effects. Contrarian to the narrative that AI/automation destroys cognitive skills: the skills taxi drivers develop remain uniquely valuable for brain health even if ride-hailing apps take the job.

title: ATProto for Distributed Systems Engineers — rethinking Twitter's protocol
description: Deep dive into ATProto's design as a federated social protocol from a distributed systems perspective. Examines how social graphs, data ownership, and interoperability can be engineered at scale.
notes: Bluesky's ATProto protocol analyzed through a distributed systems lens — relevant for understanding federated social infrastructure and the technical foundations of decentralized social media.

title: Interaction Creates Dynamical AI Behavior Absent in Isolation — Physics of AI-AI interaction
description: New physics paper models AI agents interacting: a 'boss' AI directing messages at a 'subordinate' AI creates entirely new behavioral states. Kinetic theory captures effects — how message delivery format matters. Published in cs.AI/cond-mat.
notes: Counterintuitive finding: when one AI boss-directs a subordinate while ignoring replies, the subordinate adopts a behavioral state it would never exhibit alone. A kinetic theory model explains why delivery format matters in AI-AI interactions. Highly relevant for multi-agent systems research.

title: Strategy-first synthesis planning for complex natural products with LLM agents
description: SynthEx, an agentic LLM framework, plans retrosynthetic routes to complex natural products beyond reach of conventional tools. Expert chemists judged its key steps comparable to human syntheses. Releases 1000+ routes as SynthAtlas database.
notes: Agentic AI applied to organic chemistry synthesis planning. Competing strategies, self-critique, and convergent route design. Expert human chemists treated its plans as genuine — a significant benchmark for AI scientific reasoning. Open database released.

title: Against Explainable AI in Law: Why Justifiable AI Matters — Credit Scoring Example
description: Argues against narrow 'right to explanation' in AI law. Proposes 'justifiable AI' — not just technical explanations but legal justification — as the operative way to safeguard creditor rights in automated credit scoring under EU law.
notes: Sharp counter-narrative to the XAI movement in law. Instead of demanding technical explanations (which may be impossible), argues for legal justification as the operative mechanism. Directly relevant to AI governance and behavioral econ of regulatory design.
